name: g_actorBaseClass
comment: Static class-descriptor (type-info node) of the engine's base actor class: the class that PlayerBattleActor, EnemyBattleActor and AttachVehicleActor3D register as their parent. About 130 functions walk an object's class chain until they hit this node to prove 'this is an actor' before reading its transform at +0x9C..+0xA4, so do not read the 4 bytes as a plain integer.
evidence: Idiom in every user: `cls = (**obj)(obj); for (; cls; cls = cls->f_c) if (cls == &0x7C33D4) ...` (Camera_IsTargetWithinRange 0x62DCB4 then reads obj+0x27..0x29 = +0x9C..+0xA4; Field_Action_OpenDoor 0x301FB8 uses it on the player actor; Container_FindObjectByTypeIdG 0x5F581C). The class registration helpers of PlayerBattleActor (0x6A18DC), EnemyBattleActor (0x69C68C) and AttachVehicleActor3D (0x6B5688) all store this address into descriptor+0xC = parent. 124 literal slots, 134 functions, 168 references.

name: g_enemyBattleActorClass
comment: Static class-descriptor of the battle enemy-actor class 'EnemyBattleActor' (parent = g_actorBaseClass). Battle UI/action code uses it as the type test that selects enemy actor objects; the same static initialiser also seeds the default UI palette at 0x7A3744.
evidence: The never-scheduled static constructor 0x0069C68C (Ui_InitColorPalette_7A3744) calls the class registration helper 0x002A55EC as (0x7C428C, 0x7C33D4, "EnemyBattleActor"); that helper self-links the node, stores the parent at +0xC and the name string at +0x10 - exactly the same shape as the named registrations Field_RegisterActorClass_EnemyActor (0x67C498, name 'EnemyActor'). Readers: Battle_Ui_UpdatePartyPanel 0x47D47C, maybe_Battle_ActorAction_UpdateMotion 0x433720.

name: g_enemyBattleActorNizuzerufaClass
comment: Static class-descriptor of the enemy battle-actor subclass registered as 'EnemyBattleActor_Nizuzerufa' (parent = g_enemyBattleActorClass). Battle effect/action code uses it as the type test for that boss's actor before forwarding effects to it.
evidence: Next call in 0x0069C68C: (0x7C42A0, 0x7C428C, "EnemyBattleActor_Nizuzerufa"); the following two calls register 0x7C42B4 'EnemyBattleActor_NizuzerufaArm' and 0x7C42C8/0x7C42DC '...ArmLe/ArmRi' (0x14 bytes apart), which confirms the 20-byte descriptor layout. Ten battle functions compare a class chain against this node, e.g. Battle_ActionModel_NotifyEffect 0x485108 and Actor_ApplyAttachedTargetEffect 0x4014B0.

name: maybe_g_actorDisplayOffset
comment: Three-float offset added to battle actor/effect placement: the EnemyDesertWhale class registration seeds it with (0, 0, -6.5), and maybe_Battle_CameraRangeBlend_Update adds its components to the positions it computes and copies them into the sprite/effect child it creates (child+0x31C/0x320/0x324). The object lives in BSS, so the retail image holds no value to read - the numbers come from that registration.
evidence: 0x006A6034 writes 0 / 0 / 0xC0D00000 (-6.5f) through slots 0x006A625C..0x006A6264; 0x002F1A74 reads *g/[1]/[2] into local_108[3]/local_f8/local_f4 and adds them to the positions of the children made by maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildC. 12-byte width from the three consecutive word accesses.

name: g_attachVehicleActor3DClass
comment: Static class-descriptor of the field actor class 'AttachVehicleActor3D' (parent = g_actorBaseClass). The battle action-UI handle resolver uses it to accept only objects of that class.
evidence: 0x006B5688 registers (0x7C4E14, 0x7C33D4, "AttachVehicleActor3D") through 0x002A55EC; maybe_Battle_ActionUi_ResolveHandle 0x3F4230 compares the class chain against it after the generational handle lookup in the table at 0x7B80C0 (recorded as 'matching target RTTI descriptor').

name: g_playerBattleActorClass
comment: Static class-descriptor of the battle player-actor class 'PlayerBattleActor' (parent = g_actorBaseClass), i.e. the type test for a party member's battle actor.
evidence: 0x006A18DC (Ui_RegisterStaticObject_7A3FB8) registers (0x7C5014, 0x7C33D4, "PlayerBattleActor"); four functions compare class chains against it - maybe_Actor_FindAndStartType9A 0x1CAC74, maybe_Battle_ActionModel_UpdateAttachmentVisibility 0x4853EC, maybe_Battle_ActorAction_UpdateMotion 0x433720, maybe_Battle_ActorAction_UpdateCompositeB.

name: g_battleLayoutOrigin
comment: Battle layout origin as three floats: maybe_BattleScene_LayoutUnitModel_2 places units on a line at 'origin.y' (it copies word +0x4 straight into the unit's f_a0) while x/z are computed from the unit index. The layout initialiser zeroes the whole entry.
evidence: 0x006068E8: `iVar3 = *(int *)(g_00606ad8 + 4)` then `piVar1[0x28] = iVar3` next to `piVar1[0x27] = index * spacing - offset`; slot 0x00606AD8 holds 0x7C5120 and slot 0x006792E8 does too (write side, 0x006790A8 writes 0,0,0). 12-byte stride with the four slot vectors below.

name: g_battleEntryPosition

evidence: 0x0060CD5C: `if (step == 1 && index == 0) { node->f_9c = *g_0060ceb8; node->f_a0 = puVar1[1]; node->f_a4 = puVar1[2]; }` where slot 0x0060CEB8 holds 0x7C512C; the layout initialiser 0x006790A8 writes zeros there.

name: g_battleUnitSlotPos2

evidence: 0x0060B8FC selects by index: index==2 uses slot 0x0060BBAC = 0x7C5138 (`local_34 = *g_0060bbac`). 0x006790A8 seeds the values from the literal pool (0x006792EC = -5.4f, 0x006792F0 = -2.33f).

comment: Three-float (x, 0, z) battle position of unit-layout slot 4 (0, 0, 7.24), the front-centre slot: the index==4 branch of BattleScene_ApplyUnitSlotTransform copies it into the model node's f_9c/f_a0/f_a4, and maybe_BattleScene_LayoutPartyUnits_Tail reads it too.

name: maybe_g_battleScrollOffsetTable
comment: Eight (min, max) float pairs read by maybe_Battle_Ui_UpdateScrollAnimation: entry i is fetched at +i*8 as the start/end of the scroll offset for the current item count. The same block is also written with six palette words by the static colour initialiser Field_InitActorColorTable_7A5C74, so only the float-table reading is backed by live code.
evidence: 0x0059F544: iVar2 = g_0059f7c8 then pfVar6 = (float *)(iVar2 + anim[5] * 8) and *(float *)(iVar2 + anim[5] * 8 + 4); its own header calls it an 8-entry table. 0x006AE9B0 writes *g_006aebfc and [+1..+5] with palette values.

name: maybe_g_actorListNodePoolTail
comment: Last node of the static actor-list node pool that Field_InitActorListNodePool builds: it chains the six 0x58-byte nodes at 0x7C83B4..0x7C8578 and resets this one, and every node's first word is the shared node descriptor 0x781064. The 8 visible bytes are the node's two list words.
evidence: 0x00680C54 writes six nodes 0x58 apart ending here (`g_00680e24[1] = g_00680e24 + -0x19; *puVar2 = uVar1;` with uVar1 = the 0x00781064 descriptor); its header names 0x007C8578 as the reset list head. maybe_Battle_ComputeRewardShare 0x1B7340 also passes this address (slot 0x001B750C) to the movie-surface/video-buffer constructors.

name: maybe_g_modelClass
comment: Static class-descriptor (type-info node) of the loaded model/animation instance class: every resource loader validates the object returned by the archive lookup by walking its class chain to this node before binding it, and maybe_Class_IsInstanceOf is the shared 'return it only if it is a model' helper.
evidence: Monster_LoadEnemyAnimation 0x420F84 ends with `iVar4 = g_00421134; iVar3 = (**obj)(obj); do { if (iVar3 == iVar4) return obj; iVar3 = iVar3->f_c; } while (iVar3);`; same test in BattleScene_BindUnitModelResources 0x4BA3F0 (slot 0x004BA9CC) and maybe_Class_IsInstanceOf 0x7079D0 (slot 0x00707A0C). The lazy type-info initialiser 0x691C0C sets +0xC = the parent node 0x7E2000 and +0x10/+0x14 = the code pointers 0x576E90/0x576CBC.

name: maybe_g_defaultBasisVector2
comment: Second of the five consecutive 12-byte (3-float) default-vector entries at 0x7E7000..0x7E703C that object constructors copy into new transforms; math and effect code reads it, often negated, as a box/billboard axis. The exact axis (up / forward / scale) is not verified.
evidence: 12-byte entry directly after 0x7E7000 (which other notes call the 'identity orientation' block) and before 0x7E7018/0x7E7024/0x7E7030. Read as `-*g_0015afb4`, `-g_0015afb4[1]`, `-g_0015afb4[2]` in Math_ClampPointToBox 0x15ACB0 and in Battle_Effect_ComputeSpawnTransform-style effect code; 66 literal slots, 70 functions, 245 references. Values are BSS, so they are written by a startup initialiser that was not located.
